extracted.intended_audience: legal scholars, patent lawyers, empirical researchers, and policy makers interested in patent litigation outcomes
extracted.subtask_description: Empirical/regression-based analysis of patent litigation outcomes across technologies and industries, using litigation- and patent-level covariates (e.g., summary judgment, trial results, invalidity grounds, patent characteristics, districts, and entity type).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Owner, Definitive Winner
rubrics_metrics.description: Binary indicator that the patent owner is a definitive winner (final adjudication in their favor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a primary outcome in regressions (top row = coefficient; significance levels shown). Distinguishes definitive victories from interim wins; definitive victories may include trial or dispositive summary judgment rulings that result in a final patentee win.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Owner, Trial Winner
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicator that the patent owner won at trial (bench or jury).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to measure success specifically at trial as opposed to summary adjudication; table reports coefficients and p-values for trial-winner outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentee Interim Wins
rubrics_metrics.description: Interim win recorded when summary judgment was denied and there was no further resolution on the merits (includes many settlements and pending cases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors record such cases as patentee interim wins; these are treated as patentee wins in some analyses to assess how inclusion of interim wins changes win-rate comparisons across industries. Note: coding did not always record whether such cases later settled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Win Rate (including interim wins)
rubrics_metrics.description: Win rate metric that counts patentee interim wins as patentee wins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to compare win rates across technologies (e.g., pharmaceuticals, software, mechanical, biotechnology). Including interim wins shrinks observed gaps but does not eliminate differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: SJ Invalidity, All
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicator that summary judgment found the patent invalid (any ground) at the summary judgment stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported in regression tables as a covariate/outcome. Used to examine how invalidity at summary judgment stage varies by technology and other patent/litigation characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: SJ Noninfringement plus Stipulated Judgment of Noninfringement
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary-judgment or stipulated-judgment rulings finding noninfringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treated as an important dispositive outcome; included in regressions to separate noninfringement dispositions from invalidity dispositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidity, All (Any Stage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicator that the patent was adjudicated invalid at any stage of litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as an outcome to capture patent invalidation across stages (summary judgment, trial, appeal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidity, §102 Prior Art (Any Stage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjudication of invalidity based on §102 (anticipation/prior art) at any stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included separately in regressions to identify which statutory grounds drive invalidity outcomes by technology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidity, §103 Obviousness (Any Stage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjudication of invalidity based on §103 (obviousness) at any stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported to assess how obviousness findings differ across technologies and courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidity, §112 Indefiniteness (Any Stage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjudication of invalidity for indefiniteness under §112 at any stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a separate ground of invalidity in regression specifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidity, §112 Inadequate Disclosure (Any Stage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjudication of invalidity for inadequate written description or enablement under §112 at any stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to capture disclosure-based invalidity (e.g., written description, enablement) and its prevalence by technology (noting later caselaw changes affecting biotechnology).

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct Infringement, Literal plus DOE (Any Stage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Findings of direct infringement, including literal infringement and infringement under the doctrine of equivalents (DOE), at any stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included in regression specifications as an outcome (or covariate) to analyze rates of infringement findings across technologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign Origin of Patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Dummy indicating that the patent has a foreign origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included as a covariate in regressions; reported coefficients and p-values indicate its relationship with outcomes like invalidity and patentee wins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjusted Number of Citations Received
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent-quality proxy measuring the number of forward citations adjusted (method not detailed on this page).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as an explanatory variable in regressions to proxy patent value/quality and its effect on litigation outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total Prior Art References
rubrics_metrics.description: Count of prior art references cited on the patent (total prior art references).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included as a patent-quality/control covariate in regressions; may relate to invalidity or other outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of Claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent's number of claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included as a patent characteristic in regressions; reported with coefficients indicating its association with outcomes such as invalidity findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age of Patent at Current Litigation Filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Time (age) of the patent when the current litigation was filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a covariate; older patents may have different litigation outcomes. Regression tables report coefficients and significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of Defendants
rubrics_metrics.description: Count of defendants named in the lawsuit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included in regression models; discussed qualitatively (more defendants in software cases may increase chance that at least one defendant pushes case to adjudication).

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of Asserted Patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Count of patents asserted in the lawsuit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included in regressions; affects litigation stakes and the potential for per-lawsuit vs per-patent analyses (notably in biotech analyses).

rubrics_metrics.name: Technology / Industry Area (technology dummies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Categorical dummies indicating patent/ case technology: Pharmaceuticals, Software, Mechanical, Biotechnology, Optics, Electrical, (Comparison dummy = Chemistry).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Central to the article's analysis: comparisons of win rates, invalidation rates, trial/disposition patterns by technology. Regression tables include technology dummies and F-tests for joint technology effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: District Court Fixed Effects (District Dummies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Dummy variables for specific district courts (e.g., ED Tex, D Del, ND Cal, CD Cal, SD Cal, SDNY, ND Ill, WD Wis, D NJ, D Mass, ED Va, ND Ohio, SD Tex).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included in Appendix B regressions 'including districts' to control for forum effects on outcomes; coefficients reported to show district-specific effects on patentee victories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial Type: Jury vs Bench
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicator for whether a case was a jury trial or bench trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Descriptive statistics note industry differences (pharmaceutical trials are almost all bench trials; software/mechanical/biotechnology are nearly all jury trials). Trial type may influence settlement decisions and which cases reach trial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trials without a Prior Summary Judgment Ruling
rubrics_metrics.description: Count/indicator of trials that occurred without a prior summary judgment motion being decided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported by technology (e.g., over half of pharmaceutical trials occurred without prior SJ ruling); lack of prior SJ may affect which cases reach trial and observed trial outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entity Status: Nonpracticing Entity (NPE) vs Practicing Entity
rubrics_metrics.description: Categorization of patent holder as an NPE (does not make/sell products) versus an operating/practicing company.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discussed as affecting settlement incentives (NPEs have fewer settlement options like cross-licenses, less ability to obtain injunctive relief), reputational concerns, risk aversion, and potentially the mix of cases that go to judgment; authors note mixed empirical evidence on settlement-rate differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contingent Fee Representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the plaintiff is represented on a contingent fee basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discussed as influencing case selection and settlement incentives: contingent-fee lawyers lower plaintiffs' upfront costs and may either seek early settlements or screen for stronger cases; included as a factor that could affect which cases go to judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement Frequency / Settlement Incentives
rubrics_metrics.description: Propensity of cases to settle rather than reach dispositive rulings or trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple textual discussions: settlements may be driven by design-around possibilities, transaction costs, contingent fees, and industry-specific incentives (e.g., pharmaceuticals vs software). Interim wins often reflect settlements and are counted in some analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design-Around Ease (patent covers small component)
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree to which the patented invention covers only a small component and can be designed around.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When inventions cover small components (common in smartphones), defendants can design around, reducing damages and increasing the ratio of attorneys' fees to recovery, encouraging settlement for nuisance value; discussed as a selection mechanism affecting which patents reach adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reputational Concerns of Litigants
rubrics_metrics.description: The extent to which plaintiffs (especially operating companies) face reputational constraints influencing assertion of weak patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practicing entities may avoid asserting weak patents due to reputational costs; NPEs may have fewer reputational concerns, which could affect the strength of asserted patents and settlement behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media / Academic Discourse Influence on Judges
rubrics_metrics.description: Potential extralegal influence of press and academic criticism (e.g., of software patents) on judicial decision making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors note the possibility that judges may be influenced indirectly by newspaper op-eds or personal contacts, potentially affecting outcomes by technology; cited literature on extralegal influences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Prosecution Investment / Portfolio Strength
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent of investment in patent prosecution and resulting portfolio strength.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested as a source of differences across industries: industries like pharmaceuticals may invest more per patent, producing stronger portfolios and affecting which patents are selected for litigation and their likelihood of surviving adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Per-Patent vs Per-Lawsuit Unit of Analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether analysis is conducted per-patent or per-lawsuit (e.g., per-lawsuit counts an overall case as a patentee victory if at least one patent was adjudicated valid and infringed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors perform robustness checks by transforming biotech analysis from per-patent to per-lawsuit to see if conclusions change; per-lawsuit analysis can show whether patentees 'win' at least one asserted patent in a case even if others fail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of Recent Caselaw on Patentability Standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes in judicial standards (e.g., written description, subject-matter eligibility, obviousness) and their likely effects on outcomes for certain technologies (notably biotechnology).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discussed qualitatively: Ariad (written description), Myriad (DNA eligibility), In re Kubin (obviousness) tightened standards for biotech since 2008 and may explain high invalidation rates observed for biotech patents in the sample.
